newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom keeps gas supplies to Ukraine limited.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom keeps gas supplies to Ukraine limited.

text.p: Russian Gazprom company said after talks of its head, Rem Vyakhirev, in the Ukrainian capital Kiev on Wednesday that natural gas supplies to Ukraine will be limited because of huge debt but promised a help to the former Soviet republic in creating strategic gas resources.
"It was agreed that the Ukrainian side will take all necessary steps to pay its debt to Gazprom, " Gazprom's press office said in a statement issued talks.
"Gas supplies to Intergaz and Energy Systems of Ukraine (UESU) will be limited because of debt," said the statment faxed to Reuters.
Gazprom, fed up with Ukraine not paying for the gas they consume, cut flows on Tuesday to Ukraine by about one third to around 37 million cubic metres per day.

Gazprom's statement said that despite cuts in supplies to two main private owned improters of the Russian gas, the company will continue and expand a contract on providing gas for Ukraine's stratecic resources.

Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and Vyakhirev agreed that Gazprom will meet its obligations and supply extra 5 billion cubic metres to fill Ukraine's underground gas depots, the statement said. It did not say what was the initial contract.

Ukraine, the world's single largest consumer and conveyor of Russian gas, is due this year to import 53 billion cubic metres of Russian gas. It will transport about 125 billion cubic metres via its territory to Europe.
Ukraine owes Gazprom $3.5 billion for 1992-94 supplies, including $1.4 billion already restructured for 12 years with the first $221.5 million tranche to be paid by the end of 1997.
The Energy Systems of Ukraine and the Intergaz owe Gazprom $150 million.
